body.x: BarunBio (CEO Hong Jin-gi) participated in the global media event' CES Unveiled' on January 7 (local time) before the official opening of CES 2024.

The company, known for its extensive research in micro-energy technology over a decade, has developed an advanced line of 'athleisure' apparel called 'WE-STIM' (Wearable Electric Stimulation). This product range aims to maximize user exercise performance through innovative functionalities based on micro-electric energy technology.

The leggings introduced under 'WE-STIM' were selected for an innovation award at CES 2024, proving their technological distinctiveness and market competitiveness. These leggings stand out for harvesting micro-electricity generated during daily movements without separating batteries or electrical components.

WE-STIM delivers the harvested energy to the user's muscles during exercise, promoting continuous functional activation. This results in improved exercise performance, accelerated muscle recovery, and reduced fatigue. According to actual exercise experiment results, the electrical stimulation provided by the conductive fibers in WE-STIM enhances user exercise performance by 30% and reduces muscle fatigue by an average of 6%.

Furthermore, WE-STIM aids in accelerating recovery during rest, alleviating everyday muscle pain, swelling, and more. Hong Jin-gi, CEO of BarunBio, expressed his enthusiasm about the CES Unveiled event, stating that it provided a rare opportunity to meet with foreign journalists and influencers with extensive insights into the industry.

body.cap: BarunBio representatives at the CES Unveiled site interacting with foreign press | Photo courtesy of AVING News

body.x: CEO Hong mentioned, "While there are many ways to expand contact with general consumers or customers to provide direct feedback on product satisfaction at domestic and international exhibitions, opportunities to meet with foreign journalists and influencers with broad insights into the industry are rare. We expect to obtain unexpected questions and improvement points from them."

He explained the company's decision to participate. He stated, "Although we have continued to sell the WE-STIM product line without much marketing since its launch, we plan to deploy a different promotional strategy after CES 2024 participation and innovation award selection. This participation in Unveiled is one of those plans, and we hope to make our products and technology known to more people globally through the global media."

The Consumer Technology Association (CTA) hosts CES, the world's largest IT exhibition held annually in Las Vegas, USA, allowing visitors to grasp global trends in the home appliance industry at a glance. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been reporting CES news worldwide since 2006 and selecting the best innovative products, companies, and technologies through 'BEST OF CES' and 'BEST OF MADE IN KOREA.' Additionally, through 'AVING LIVE,' they deliver real-time CES issues.

The CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion is being operated on the most historical scale since Seoul's first participation in CES in 2020, with the largest exhibition area, number of participating companies, and supporter numbers. The Seoul Pavilion, which has collaborated with 13 institutions, is essential in Seoul's endeavors to establish itself as a startup hub. Among the participating companies in the Seoul Pavilion, 17 received innovation awards, proving their capabilities. Participating institutions include SBA, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul Campus Town, Yangjae Innovation Hub, Gwanak-gu, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, and Kyunghee University, totaling 13. Seoul City and institutions and supporters participating in industry-academic cooperation are matched 1:1 with companies, with a maximum of 85 supporters participating.
